title: Order lifecycle and statuses
content:
| Status | Set by | Customer sees | Means |
|---|---|---|---|
| `received` | checkout | Order received | Payment authorised, not yet paid |
| `paid` | payment processor | Order confirmed | Funds captured; the order enters the pick queue |
| `held-verification` | fraud rules | Order on hold | Over £400 to a non-billing address; a call is due |
| `held-stock` | stock system | Awaiting stock | One or more lines short at pick |
| `picking` | goods in | Being prepared | On a picker's list |
| `packed` | goods in | Being prepared | Boxed, labelled, waiting for the carrier |
| `dispatched` | carrier scan | Dispatched | Carrier has it; tracking is live |
| `delivered` | carrier scan | Delivered | Carrier has recorded delivery |
| `collection-ready` | workshop | Ready to collect | At the workshop counter, held fourteen days |
| `cancelled` | support or customer | Cancelled | No goods shipped; refund due |
| `returned` | returns desk | Return received | Graded, refund authorised or escalated |
| `closed` | nightly job | (nothing) | Ninety days after delivery with no open ticket |

title: Order lifecycle and statuses
content:
The pick queue is ordered by the time the order reached `paid`, not by the time
the customer clicked buy. An order held for verification loses its place only
for the duration of the hold; when it is released it goes back in at its
original payment time rather than at the back.

Trade orders sit in the same queue as retail orders. There is no priority in
either direction and there never has been, whatever a customer has been told.

title: Order lifecycle and statuses
content:
A line that cannot be picked puts the whole order into `held-stock`. Fulfilment
then chooses one of three things, and tells the customer which:

1. **Split the order.** Ship what is available now and the rest when it lands.
   No extra delivery charge. This is the default when the missing line is more
   than three days out.
2. **Hold the order.** Ship everything together when the stock arrives. Chosen
   when the missing line is due within three days.
3. **Cancel the line.** Refund it and ship the rest. Chosen when there is no
   arrival date.

We never substitute a different part for a short line, and we never guess an
arrival date. "We do not have a date" is an acceptable thing to say and an
invented date is not.

title: Order lifecycle and statuses
content:
A customer can cancel any time before `picking`. Between `picking` and
`dispatched` we will try, and we will be honest that we may not catch it. After
`dispatched` it is a return, and the returns policy applies.

An order cancelled before dispatch is refunded in full including delivery,
within five working days.

title: Order lifecycle and statuses
content:
Order confirmation at `paid`. Dispatch confirmation with tracking at
`dispatched`. A collection-ready email at `collection-ready`, followed by a
reminder on day seven and a final one on day thirteen.

Nothing is emailed at `picking`, `packed` or `closed`. A customer who asks why
they got no email between confirmation and dispatch has found the answer, not a
bug.

title: Order lifecycle and statuses
content:
A status describes where an order is, not when it will arrive. Delivery
estimates come from the shipping policy and from the carrier, and a support
reply should quote the estimate rather than reading a date off the status
screen.

title: Returns and refunds
content:
**Customers may return an unused item within 30 days of delivery for a full
refund.** The item must be unfitted, in resaleable condition, and in its
original packaging with any tags, backing card or instruction sheet still with
it.

Thirty days is a policy, not a statutory minimum, and it is deliberately longer
than the statutory cooling-off period so that nobody has to count weekends.

title: Returns and refunds
content:
A part is unfitted if it has not been mounted on a bicycle. In practice:

- A caliper that has been bolted on, even briefly, is fitted.
- A cassette that has been on a freehub body has almost always marked the
  splines and is fitted.
- A chain that has been sized or run through a drivetrain is fitted.
- Tyres are fitted the moment they have been on a rim. A tyre that has been
  test-fitted and removed will show bead marks and we will see them.
- A frame that has had a bottom bracket or headset pressed into it is fitted.
- Clothing and helmets may be tried on. A helmet with a scuffed shell or a
  compressed liner is not resaleable.

If you are not sure whether fitting a part will cost you the return, ask before
you fit it. The answer is usually yes.

title: Returns and refunds
content:
- Anything cut to length: cables, outers, hydraulic hose, steerer tubes, bar
  tape that has been unwound and applied.
- Tubeless sealant and any opened liquid.
- Special-order items, which are marked as such on the product page before the
  order is placed.
- Gift vouchers.
- Anything returned without its original packaging where that packaging is part
  of how we resell it — a boxed wheelset, for example.

title: Returns and refunds
content:
1. Start a return at `www.braxbycycles.example/returns` with the order number
   and the email address on the order.
2. Print the prepaid label. UK returns are free. Republic of Ireland and EU
   returns are at the customer's cost unless the item is faulty.
3. Pack the item as it arrived and attach the label to the outside of the
   outer box, not to the product box.
4. Drop it at any carrier point.

title: Returns and refunds
content:
A refund is issued to the original payment method within five working days of
the return arriving at the returns unit. Card refunds usually clear within a
further three working days; that part is the bank's timetable, not ours.

We refund the original outbound standard delivery charge when the whole order
is returned. We do not refund the difference where the customer chose next-day
delivery, and we do not refund the outbound charge on a partial return.

title: Returns and refunds
content:
We do not process exchanges as a single transaction. Return the item for a
refund and place a new order. This is slower to describe and faster in
practice, because the new order ships as soon as it is placed rather than
waiting for the return to arrive.

title: Returns and refunds
content:
A faulty item is not a return, it is a warranty claim, and the warranty policy
governs it. The practical difference for the customer is that carriage is
always ours and the 30-day window does not apply.

If an item arrives damaged in transit, tell us within three working days of
delivery so that we can raise it with the carrier. After that the carrier will
not accept the claim and we have to treat it as a warranty question instead,
which is slower for everyone.

title: Returns and refunds
content:
Trade returns are governed by the trade account terms and not by this document.
The headline difference is that trade returns of non-stock items carry a
restocking charge.

title: Recommended service intervals
content:
**Hydraulic disc brakes should be bled every 12 months.** Mineral oil and DOT
fluid both take on water over time, and a lever that has gone slightly long
over a season is usually a fluid problem rather than a pad problem.

**Hydraulic disc brakes used for wet-weather commuting should be bled every 6
months.** Year-round commuting, winter road riding and regular wet gravel all
count. The mechanism is the same; the rate is roughly double.

Pads are inspected every 500 km and replaced at 1 mm of friction material
remaining above the backing plate. Rotors are replaced at 1.5 mm thickness.

Rim brakes: pads inspected every 500 km, cables and outers replaced every 12
months, and the braking surface checked against the manufacturer's wear
indicator at every service.

title: Recommended service intervals
content:
| Task | Interval |
|---|---|
| Chain wear check | Every 1,000 km |
| Chain replacement | At 0.5% elongation on an 11- or 12-speed chain |
| Cassette replacement | Typically every third chain |
| Chainring inspection | Every 3,000 km |
| Gear cable and outer replacement | Every 12 months, or every 6 months for winter use |
| Derailleur hanger alignment check | At every service and after any fall |

A chain replaced on time is the cheapest maintenance there is. A chain replaced
late takes the cassette with it, and often the chainrings after that.

title: Recommended service intervals
content:
Wheel true and tension check every 2,000 km. A new wheel or a workshop-built
wheel should come back at 300 km for a first re-tension; spokes bed in and the
first check is not optional if the warranty on the build is to hold.

Hub bearings: inspected every 5,000 km, serviced or replaced when there is
detectable play or roughness. Sealed cartridge bearings are replaced rather
than serviced.

Tubeless sealant is topped up every 3 months and replaced entirely every 6
months. A tyre that has been standing unridden for a season will usually need
the sealant scraped out rather than topped up.

title: Recommended service intervals
content:
Headset service every 12 months. **Headsets on bikes ridden through the winter
should be serviced every 6 months**, because the failure is corrosion in the
lower bearing race and it is driven by road salt rather than by distance.

Bottom bracket inspected every 5,000 km. Seatpost removed, cleaned and
regreased every 12 months — on carbon frames, with assembly compound rather
than grease, and to the frame manufacturer's torque figure.

Bolt torque check across the whole bike every 6 months, and always after
travelling with the bike disassembled.

title: Recommended service intervals
content:
The workshop's full service is a fixed list, and it is on the workshop price
list. It includes a bleed, a drivetrain clean and measure, a wheel true and
tension, a headset and bottom bracket check, a bolt torque check, and a gear
and brake set-up. It does not include parts, and it does not include a wheel
rebuild.

title: Recommended service intervals
content:
Anything that has hit the ground hard comes in for an inspection before it goes
back out, whatever the intervals above say. The specific checks are the
derailleur hanger, the bar and stem for creases and marks, the frame at the
head tube and the down tube, and the wheels for a flat spot. Carbon components
that have taken an impact are replaced rather than inspected and passed.

title: Shipping and delivery
content:
Braxby Cycles ships to the United Kingdom, the Republic of Ireland and the
European Union. We do not ship anywhere else, and the checkout will not accept
an address outside those territories.

title: Shipping and delivery
content:
Standard delivery is priced by the weight of the whole basket, in three bands.

| Basket weight | Standard delivery |
|---|---|
| Up to 2 kg | £3.99 |
| Over 2 kg and up to 10 kg | £6.99 |
| Over 10 kg | £11.99 |

**Standard UK delivery is free on orders over £60.** The threshold is the order
value after any discount and before delivery, so a £62 basket with a 10%
discount code applied does not qualify.

Standard delivery is two to three working days. It is not a tracked service
below 2 kg; above 2 kg it is.

Next-day delivery is £7.99 regardless of weight, for orders placed before 14:00
Monday to Friday. An order placed at 14:01 on a Friday is picked on Monday and
delivered on Tuesday. We say this plainly because it is the single most common
complaint the support inbox receives.

We do not deliver on Sundays. Saturday delivery is available on the next-day
service for orders placed before 14:00 on a Friday, at £11.99.

title: Shipping and delivery
content:
A flat £9.99, three to five working days, tracked. Duties and taxes are paid by
us; the customer pays nothing on delivery.

title: Shipping and delivery
content:
A flat £14.99, four to seven working days, tracked, delivered duty paid. Some
destinations are slower than the stated band and we do not guarantee the upper
figure for the islands.

title: Shipping and delivery
content:
Orders can be collected from the Manchester workshop. Collection is free, there
is no minimum order, and the order is held for fourteen days. Collection is
available during workshop hours only, which are in the staff handbook and on
the workshop booking page — the trade counter and the workshop keep the same
hours.

The workshop closes on 14 August each year for stock-taking. Online orders are
unaffected and ship as normal from the Marbury Trading Estate unit; only
collections and workshop bookings are affected.

title: Shipping and delivery
content:
Complete bikes, framesets and boxed wheelsets ship on a two-person service
where the carrier requires it. This can add a working day and it is quoted at
the £11.99 band rather than separately.

We cannot ship pressurised items — CO2 cartridges, sealed shocks — by air, so
those lines are UK and Republic of Ireland only.

title: Shipping and delivery
content:
Tracked services: raise it with us once the tracking has not moved for two
working days. Untracked services: we ask customers to wait ten working days
from dispatch before we treat a parcel as lost, because that is the point at
which the carrier will accept a claim.

A parcel marked as delivered but not received is a carrier investigation and
takes up to seven working days. We do not send a replacement before the
investigation closes, except on orders under £30, where we replace immediately
and absorb it.

title: Shipping and delivery
content:
We ship to any address in the permitted territories. Orders over £400 going to
an address other than the card's billing address are held for a verification
call. That call is made within one working day, and the order does not lose its
place in the pick queue while we make it.

title: Warranty policy
content:
These terms are used consistently throughout the rest of the policy, and the
categories in section 6 depend on them.

**Component.** Any item sold as a single part or as a boxed set of parts, in the
condition it left our supplier. A caliper, a cassette, a wheelset in its factory
packaging, a frameset in its factory packaging.

**Consumable.** A part designed to wear out in normal use. The list is closed
and appears in section 4.

**Workshop-built assembly.** Anything the Manchester workshop has assembled,
laced, tensioned, bled, faced or aligned before it left us. A wheel laced and
tensioned by the workshop is a workshop-built assembly, whether or not the rim
and the hub were bought from Braxby Cycles. A complete bike built to order in
the workshop is a workshop-built assembly. A wheelset that arrived boxed from
the supplier and was shipped on unopened is not — that is a component.

**Bare frame.** A frame or frameset sold on its own, with or without a fork,
with no drivetrain, wheels or contact points fitted.

**Complete bike.** A bicycle sold ready to ride, whether built in the workshop
or shipped boxed from a supplier.

title: Warranty policy
content:
Braxby Cycles covers manufacturing defects and defects in materials. In
practice that means a part that fails in normal use without having been
crashed, modified, corroded through neglect, or fitted outside the
manufacturer's stated limits.

A claim needs three things: the order number, a description of how the part
failed, and photographs. The workshop will ask for the part itself in most
cases, and Customer Operations will send a prepaid label when it does.

title: Warranty policy
content:
- Damage from a crash, an impact, or a fall.
- Damage from a fitting error, whether by the customer or by a third-party
  mechanic. Work carried out in our own workshop is covered by section 7.
- Corrosion, seizure or wear caused by a lack of maintenance. The maintenance
  we expect is the schedule in the service intervals document.
- Cosmetic marks, paint chips, and finish wear that do not affect function.
- Any part that has been modified, re-drilled, re-faced by a third party, or
  refinished.
- Loss of performance that is ordinary wear. A brake pad that is thin, a chain
  that has stretched, or a tyre that has worn through its tread indicator is a
  consumable at end of life, not a defect.

title: Warranty policy
Warranty policy
content:
Crash replacement is a discretionary scheme, separate from warranty, and it
exists because a frame that has been crashed is not a defective frame.

**Bare frames purchased from Braxby Cycles are covered by the crash-replacement
scheme.** A customer who crashes a bare frame bought from us within thirty-six
months of the order date can buy a replacement frame of the same model, or the
nearest current equivalent, at forty per cent off the published price.

**Frames supplied as part of a complete bike are not covered by the
crash-replacement scheme.** The frame in a complete bike is not sold as a
separate line, so there is no frame order to date the scheme from, and the
discount is not offered. This has caught customers out and it is worth saying
plainly at the point of sale.

The scheme is discretionary. The workshop inspects the damage, confirms it is
consistent with an impact rather than with a defect, and Customer Operations
approves or declines. A declined crash-replacement request does not prevent a
warranty claim on the same frame if the workshop's inspection suggests one.

title: Warranty policy
content:
The term runs from the date the order was delivered, not from the date it was
placed, and not from the date the customer first rode it.

| Category | Term | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Components | 24 months | The default. Everything not named below. |
| Wickhaven frames and rigid forks | 60 months | Original purchaser only, non-transferable. |
| Workshop-built assemblies | 36 months | Covers the build itself: spoke tension, bearing preload, hose routing, facing and alignment. |
| Electronics and lighting | 24 months | Batteries are covered against defect, not against capacity loss. |
| Consumables | none | See section 4. |
| Trade account orders | 12 months | Trade terms override this table; see the trade account terms. |

A workshop-built assembly that fails because of a defective component is
handled as a component claim, on the component's term. The two terms sit
alongside each other and the customer gets the benefit of whichever is longer.

title: Warranty policy
section: Work carried out in our workshop
content:
Labour carried out by the Manchester workshop is guaranteed for twelve months.
If a bleed will not hold, a wheel goes out of true under normal use, or a
bearing preload backs off, bring it back and we redo the work at no charge.

There is one exception, and it is absolute: **where the customer supplied the
part, the labour guarantee does not apply.** The workshop cannot stand behind a
build using a component it did not sell and cannot inspect the provenance of.
The workshop service terms set out which customer-supplied parts we will fit at
all.

title: Warranty policy
content:
1. Email `support@braxbycycles.example` with the order number and photographs.
2. Customer Operations acknowledges within one working day and either resolves
   it or raises a workshop inspection.
3. Where the part is needed, a prepaid label is issued and the part is sent to
   the returns unit at Marbury Trading Estate, Manchester.
4. A decision is issued within ten working days of the part arriving.
5. An approved claim is settled by replacement where we hold stock, by credit
   where we do not, and by refund where neither is possible.

We do not charge an inspection fee, and we do not charge return carriage on a
claim that is approved. A claim that is declined and where the customer wants
the part back is returned at our cost once; after that we hold the part for
sixty days and then dispose of it.

title: Workshop service bulletins, 2026
content:
All torque wrenches on the bench are now sent for calibration every six months
rather than annually. Two wrenches were found out of tolerance during the
December audit, both reading low, which is the direction that produces
under-torqued stem bolts and a customer who comes back.

Calibration stickers carry the due date. A wrench past its date does not get
used, and there is no judgement call available here.

---

title: Workshop service bulletins, 2026
content:
Hookless rims have a hard pressure ceiling and a narrow list of approved tyres.
Do not set up a tubeless tyre on a hookless rim unless the tyre is on the rim
manufacturer's approved list, and do not exceed the rim's stated maximum
pressure even if the tyre is rated higher.

If the customer insists on a tyre that is not on the list, decline the job and
explain why. Record the refusal on the job sheet.

---

title: Workshop service bulletins, 2026
content:
The service intervals document now calls for a six-month bleed on bikes used
for wet-weather commuting. Workshop staff should ask the question at booking —
"is this a year-round bike?" — and set the next-service reminder accordingly
rather than defaulting to twelve months.

The reminder is set in the job system at the point the job is closed, not at
the point it is booked.

---

title: Workshop service bulletins, 2026
section: 2026-04 — Rear caliper mount adapters, Halvard R4
content:
A recurring error on the bench: fitting a 160 mm rear rotor to a frame with a
post mount designed for 180 mm, and then reaching for a generic adapter to make
up the difference.

Use the correct adapter. For a Halvard R4 rear caliper going from a 160 mm
mount to a 180 mm rotor, the part is **BRK-1180**. It is the only rear adapter
we stock that has the correct offset for the R4 caliper body, and it ships with
the two longer bolts the conversion needs. A generic post-mount adapter will
bolt up and will hold the caliper a millimetre out of plane, which is why those
bikes come back with a rub the customer can hear and the mechanic cannot find.

Front conversions use ADP-3308 and are unaffected.

If the part is out of stock, the job waits. Do not substitute.

---

title: Workshop service bulletins, 2026
content:
The 0.5% gauges have replaced the 0.75% gauges on all three benches. Eleven-
and twelve-speed chains are replaced at 0.5% elongation, and a chain that
passes the old gauge has usually already started on the cassette.

Old gauges have been removed from the workshop. If you find one in a toolbox,
bin it.

---

title: Workshop service bulletins, 2026
content:
A reminder rather than a change. The workshop service terms are clear that we
do not fit customer-supplied braking components of any kind, and that includes
pads that a customer has bought from us previously and brought back on a
different bike.

Three jobs were accepted against this rule in the first quarter. All three were
completed and none of them caused a problem, which is exactly why the rule
needs restating: nothing going wrong is not evidence that the rule was wrong.

---

title: Workshop service bulletins, 2026
content:
The workshop closes on 14 August for stock-taking, as it does every year. No
bookings are taken for that day. Bikes already in the workshop are secured and
not worked on. Online orders are unaffected and ship as normal from the goods-
in unit.

Any job scheduled for the closure day is moved to the following working day,
and the customer is called rather than emailed.

title: Workshop service terms
content:
Book online at `www.braxbycycles.example/workshop` or at the counter. We hold
slots for two working days after a booking is made and release them if the bike
has not arrived.

Bikes are booked in by the half day. A bike dropped off without a booking goes
into the queue behind everything already booked, and in season that can be two
weeks.

title: Workshop service terms
content:
This is the section customers argue with most, so it is stated as two rules
with no exceptions between them.

**The workshop will fit customer-supplied tyres, inner tubes, saddles,
seatposts, bar tape, pedals and bottle cages.** These are parts where a fitting
error is visible immediately, where the part cannot fail in a way that hurts
somebody a week later, and where we can inspect the part on the bench and see
what we are dealing with.

**The workshop will not fit customer-supplied disc brake pads, hydraulic hoses,
calipers, levers, rotors or any other braking component.** We have no way to
verify the compound, the backing plate, the hose fitting standard or the
provenance, and a brake that fails is not a brake that fails visibly. This is
not negotiable and the counter staff are told to decline it politely and
without discussion.

Customer-supplied drivetrain parts, wheels and frames are at the workshop
manager's discretion, decided on the bench, and declined without argument if
the part looks wrong for the bike.

Where the customer supplied the part, the labour guarantee in the warranty
policy does not apply. We will still put right our own mistake, but we will not
carry the risk of a part we did not sell.

title: Workshop service terms
content:
Every job gets a written quotation before work starts. If the work turns out to
need more than the quotation, we stop and call. We will not exceed a quotation
by more than £20 without speaking to the customer first, and we will not
proceed at all on a job where the extra work changes what the bike is for.

A customer who cannot be reached gets the bike back in the state it was in,
with the diagnostic time charged at the standard labour rate and nothing else.

title: Workshop service terms
content:
Bikes are stored free for fourteen days after the completion call. After
fourteen days we charge storage per day. After ninety days, and after three
recorded attempts to contact the customer, we treat the bike as abandoned and
dispose of it under the Torts (Interference with Goods) Act. We have done this
twice in eleven years and would rather never do it again.

title: Workshop service terms
content:
- We do not repair carbon frames or carbon components. We inspect them, and we
  refer them to a specialist repairer.
- We do not service internal-gear hubs beyond removing and refitting the wheel.
- We do not service electronic drivetrains beyond firmware updates, battery
  replacement and cable routing.
- We do not build wheels with customer-supplied second-hand spokes.
- We do not paint, respray or refinish.

title: Workshop service terms
content:
The workshop will decline a bike that is unsafe to work on: a cracked frame, a
seized steerer, a frame that has been repaired by an unknown party, or a bike
that arrives in a condition where the mechanic cannot get to the fasteners
without unreasonable cleaning. We will say so at the counter, we will explain
why, and we will not charge for looking.

title: Workshop service terms
content:
Twelve months, as set out in the warranty policy. Bring it back and we redo it.
The exception for customer-supplied parts, above, is the only exception.
